title: Rufinus’s book-III note; free will (III pref–1)
english: Rufinus notes he finished Books I–II under pressure in Lent and moves more slowly through III–IV. The treatise turns to free decision: praise and blame, commandments, and apostolic warnings only make sense if the rational creature is [[self-determining >> Bible:Deuteronomy 30:19]], not moved as a mere tool.

added_allusions.reason: left to the decision of his tongue

translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 22 (1913) Rufinus Latin; disclose Rufinus paraphrase.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; no ANF Crombie / Butterworth.

Rufinus preface to Book III disclosed as translator’s voice.

title: Opposing powers; double-soul claim (III.2–4)
english: Hostile powers war against the human race as Scripture says, yet they do not cancel free decision. The claim of two souls in one person is weighed and refused where it would split the human being into two agents of equal standing.

title: World began in time; end — BOOK III CLOSEOUT
english: The world began in time under God’s will; an endless series of unmade worlds is refused. The end looks toward God being all in all without making creature equal to Creator. BOOK III CLOSEOUT.
